macros.name: etocarticlestyle
macros.doc: \etocarticlestyle instructs etoc to use \section*{\contentsname} (with marks on the page) and \etocbookstyle says to use \chapter*{\contentsname}.

macros.name: etocchecksemptiness
macros.doc: The command \etocchecksemptiness tells etoc to not print, from that point on, the headings of the local tables of contents if they have empty contents.

macros.name: etocclasstocstyle
macros.doc: \etocclasstocstyle sets the ‘main toc layout’ to be as without \usepackage{etoc}.

macros.name: etocdisplay
macros.doc: Issue \etocdisplay to return to the default situation that \localtableofcontents and variants issue a \par to switch to vertical mode before typesetting the TOC title and contents.

macros.name: etocetoclocaltocstyle
macros.doc: \etocetoclocaltocstyle (package default) Activates a heading style for local tables of contents (and “lists of”) which tries to adapt automatically to the surrounding level.

macros.name: etocfallbacklines
macros.doc: \etocfallbacklines sets the ‘content lines’ to use etoc pre-defined ones.

macros.name: etocframedmphook
macros.doc: The \etocframedmphook is positioned immediately after the beginning of a minipage environment where the contents of the framed TOC are typeset.

macros.name: etocifwasempty
macros.doc: The command \etocifwasempty{⟨YES⟩}{⟨NO⟩} executes ⟨YES⟩ if the previous TOC was found to be empty and ⟨NO⟩ if its was not so.

macros.name: etocignoredepthtags
macros.doc: After \etocignoredepthtags, the .toc depth tags are ignored (but \etocdepthtag.toc still works).

macros.name: etocinline
macros.doc: With \etocinline, or its synonym \etocnopar, the \localtableofcontents command and its variants do not first issue a \par to close the previous paragraph.

macros.name: etocinnertopsep
macros.doc: An important dimension used by all three of \etocmulticolstyle, \etocruledstyle and \etocframedstyle is \etocinnertopsep. It gives the amount of separation between the heading and the start of the contents.

macros.name: etoclocallistoffigureshook
macros.doc: During expansion of \locallistoffigures or \locallistoftables, the macros \etoclocallistoffigureshook resp. \etoclocallistoftableshook are executed right before typesetting the entries.

macros.name: etoclocallistoftableshook
macros.doc: During expansion of \locallistoffigures or \locallistoftables, the macros \etoclocallistoffigureshook resp. \etoclocallistoftableshook are executed right before typesetting the entries.

macros.name: etoclocaltop
macros.doc: Within either the TOC style (\etocsettocstyle) or the local title styles (\etocsetlinestyle), the control sequence \etoclocaltop is made equivalent for the duration of \localtableofcontents to a numeric (self-delimiting) denotation of the current top level.

macros.name: etocnopar
macros.doc: With \etocinline, or its synonym \etocnopar, the \localtableofcontents command and its variants do not first issue a \par to close the previous paragraph.

macros.name: etocobeydepthtags
macros.doc: The commands \etocobeydepthtags (which is default behavior) and \etocignoredepthtags can be used to control which TOC obey depth tags.

macros.name: etocscrartclstyle
macros.doc: \etocscrartclstyle trying to emulate the global display style of the \tableofcontents within the class scrartcl.

macros.name: etocsettagdepth
macros.doc: When typesetting a TOC, one issues a series of commands \etocsettagdepth{⟨tag_name⟩}{⟨level⟩} where the ⟨level⟩ may be either numeric (from -3 to 5) or the name of a division unit known to etoc, or none or all.

macros.name: etocsettocstyle
macros.doc: \etocsettocstyle is for styling the titles (and all things related to material before and after the actual TOC contents).

macros.name: etocstandardlines
macros.doc: \etocstandardlines (package default) Sets the ‘content lines’ to be as without \usepackage{etoc}.

macros.name: etocthemaxlevel
macros.doc: The macro \etocthemaxlevel expands accordingly to either 6 (default) or 12 (if option ‘deeplevels’).

macros.name: etoctoccontentsline
macros.doc: The etoc command \etoctoccontentsline{..}{..} is provided as a substitute to \addcontentsline{toc}{..}{..}: this is to avoid the patching which is done by hyperref to \addcontentsline in its process of creation of bookmarks.

macros.name: etoctoclines
macros.doc: \etoctoclines sets the ‘content lines’ to match the last encountered \etocsetlinestyle specs.

macros.name: etocusertocstyle
macros.doc: \etocusertocstyle means to obey the \etocsettocstyle configuration as previously in place, not only for the main TOC but also for local ones.

macros.name: localtableofcontents
macros.doc: \localtableofcontents will print local tables of contents: i.e. all sections and sub-units inside a given chapter, or all subsubsections and lower inside a given subsection, etc...
